C-STARTUP-QUESTIONNAIRE.Summary: Replace Preferences and Sync with a full-screen first-start questionnaire and r to reopen it, with explicit optional answers, real Dropbox authorization, and descriptive repository names.
C-STARTUP-QUESTIONNAIRE.Problem: Startup reads currently create a default preferences row, preventing reliable first-start detection. Separate Preferences and Sync screens do not provide the requested optional setup flow, and identity repository interfaces have generic names.

Goals.Goal: Show the questionnaire automatically only when no preferences row exists, and allow r to reopen it from records.
Ask for preferred weight unit using an input and choices 1. kg and 2. lb, with an Enter-to-skip/default hint; then ask for identity provider with choice 1. Dropbox and an Enter-to-skip/no-save hint.
Implement real Dropbox account authorization with a browser and code input, using PKCE and encrypted credential persistence.
Persist only explicitly answered settings after completion. Skipping all questions or cancelling without completion does not write application rows.
Remove the separate Preferences and Sync screens and their p/s routing, and name each repository interface and implementation after its corresponding model and file.

Constraints.Constraint: Keep the questionnaire in the alternate terminal screen and fill available dimensions with main-view border styling and spacing; support resizing and compact/tiny sizes.
Reading missing preferences returns a valid in-memory kg default and a presence flag without inserting a row. Existing saved preferences suppress automatic startup setup.

Answers remain pending until questionnaire completion. Empty Enter skips that question. All skipped answers produce zero preference, identity, and credential writes. r opens the flow without deleting existing preferences or accounts.

Skipping the unit on reset retains the existing saved unit. An explicit unit selection is applied to displayed weights only after successful completion. Skipping provider leaves identities and credentials unchanged.

Dropbox uses the authorization-code flow with S256 PKCE, offline access, and an app key configured through the environment. Omit redirect_uri so the user can paste the displayed authorization code; no client secret is embedded.

OAuth code exchange runs asynchronously with cancellation and timeout. Browser-launch failure offers the authorization URL for manual opening. Invalid input, denied authorization, missing configuration, token errors, and persistence failures leave the questionnaire usable without silently creating identity rows.

Use the verified Dropbox account ID. Encrypt access and refresh tokens using authenticated encryption and a local key file with restricted permissions; do not show, log, or save plaintext tokens. Save selected preferences and linked account/credentials together through the transaction runner.

Rename identity.Repository to IdentityRepository and identity.CredentialsRepository to IdentityCredentialsRepository. Give the SQLite credential repository its own corresponding file and type; use existing transaction context for all identity and credential operations.

Preserve existing workout data, domain constructor invariants, ge/gs navigation, dialogs, help-return behavior, and global quit shortcuts. Use repository Go formatting and semantic markup conventions.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Implement remote workout synchronization, additional providers, token refresh scheduling, or an account-management screen.
Delete existing preferences or identities when opening/resetting the questionnaire, or create a preferences row merely to mark skipped setup complete.
Perform a real Dropbox authorization using the developer's account during automated verification or alter the real user database.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: A fresh temporary database opens the full-screen unit question before records, shows 1. kg and 2. lb and the skip/default hint, then shows the Dropbox provider question and skip/no-save hint.

Entering no answers and pressing Enter through both questions opens records with kg in memory and leaves preferences, identities, and credentials tables empty. The questionnaire appears again on a later startup while preferences remain absent.
Entering 1 or 2 and confirming with Enter selects kg or lb. After finishing the provider step, only the explicit unit is saved if provider is skipped; later startups go directly to records.

Choosing Dropbox starts browser authorization and a code-entry step. A successful mocked exchange saves the verified account and encrypted credentials; denied, invalid, cancelled, or failed exchanges do not save them. Linking alone does not create a skipped preferences row.

r reopens the questionnaire from records and retains browsing state. Skipping or cancelling it preserves existing settings and identities, and no r/p/s actions intercept dialog text or help-owned input.
Preferences and Sync view files, obsolete tests, and p/s help entries are removed. Help documents r to reopen setup; ge/gs remain intact.
Every repository interface and implementation has a descriptive model-prefixed Repository name matching its source file, including IdentityRepository and IdentityCredentialsRepository.

Tests cover row-presence detection, write-free defaults, skip/partial/complete/reset/cancel flows, invalid input, exact full-screen bounds and cursor position, PKCE/token exchange/encryption, atomic rollback, and preserved records navigation.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Temporary SQLite integration tests verify first-start/reset behavior, absence of implicit writes, selective persistence, and rollback without opening the real database.

Injected browser and HTTP transport tests verify the real PKCE flow and encrypted storage without contacting a live account. Rendering and interaction tests verify full-screen setup, resize/cursor bounds, and record-state retention.
Review intentional help snapshot changes, then validate normally without UPDATE_GOLDEN=1. GRACE final assertions verify replacement projections and descriptive repository names.

Assumptions.Assumption: The user explicitly approves specification and plan creation and sequential execution in this request.
Dropbox app configuration is supplied via DROPBOX_APP_KEY. A manual code-entry flow avoids requiring a registered local callback URL.
Skipping all setup means no preferences row is created, so automatic setup repeats on subsequent starts until an explicit unit preference is saved.
